You must finally flee from this impious world; when you lay down mortality, and the body is to be committed to the squalid earth: but not even here is there anything for you to fear. That Jesus of yours fled first into the land of death, from which he returned: therefore your body also will return. Let it remain there, until the Lord shall say: The Lord will come, will come with the voice of the Archangel, who will call you back from the earth, and we shall joyfully sing: Death is swallowed up in victory!

Latin:

Continuatio.

Vidimus in superiori disputatione Christi emicantem Majestatem, ex solenni Magorum adoratione: in præsenti contemplabimur summam ejus humilitatem, ex tyrannicâ Herodis persecutione. Ecce enim vix mundi lucem aspexerat lucis autor & dator, & fictâ bene volentiâ premitur; vix in propria venerat, & terrâ exire cogitur, terrarum Dominus. O rem mirandam & stupendam! (a) Si refugium fugit, si timet virtus, si præsidium migrat: qua vita? quæ spes? quæ securitas? quod munimen? Spera optimè! nec in fuga fugit salus: nec Salvator ex fuga infirmus. Non enim timidus fugit puerulus nostef truculentæ cædis hominem, sed volens: fugit (b) non formidine humanâ, sed dispensatione divinâ, non necessitate, sed potestate: (c) ut cederet tempori, non Herodi. Hoc ut clariùs patescat, FUGAM Salvatoris in Ægyptum considerandam suscipimus: cujus 1. Circumstantias expendemus. 2. Quæstiones controversas, si quæ occurrunt, subjiciemus. 3. Meditationem practicam annectemus. Tu Christe mentem & calamum rege!

Thesis I.

Circumstantias fugæ Servatoris nostri Jesu Christi, in Ægyptum, varias notat Evangelista; D. Matthæus v. 13. 14. & 15. cap. 2. Historiæ suæ Evangelicæ, quas nos ad duas principales reducimus classes si alias circumstantias personarum, alias rerum, dicimus.

II. Personæ nobis in textu Evengelio denominantur triplices: I. Angelus fugam svadens : ἰδὲ ἄγγελος κυρίου, ubi observari debet, 1. Angelicæ personæ descriptio: Angelus Domini : prim. enim nomen, officium, posterius dignitatem legati describit. Quis hic Angelorum fuerit? à nonnullis qværitur. Nos de incertis nihil certi pronunciamus, probabile tamen est, qvòd opinatur Origenes fuisse Gabrielem, qvi fidelis fuit mysteriorum Christi interpres. 2. Observanda Angelicæ apparitio: φαίνεται κατ᾽ ὄναρ. Non vigilanti apparet Angelus Josepho, ut (a) Manoah & (b) Zachariæ, sed dormienti, qvòd nos non Josephi perfectioni, ut (c) Eccius; sed liberæ Dei dispensationi adscribimus. 3. Angelicæ præceptio : ἐγερθεὶς, & παράλαβε &c. Non Josephi arbitrio relinqvit Angelus fugam, sed severè præcipit : Surge, inqvit, assume, &c.

III. Qværi hîc loci potest: An DEUS & hodiè per somnia nobiscum agat? Simpliciter hoc affirmant Legenda & praxis Papistarum, qvi ex somniis articulos fidei fabricarunt, & suas de purgatorio & indulgentiis ineptias apparitionibus nocturnis ineptè fundarunt, ut videre est apud B. (d) Chemnitium. Nos distingvimus inter res vitæ & res fidei: de istis, non de his homines per somnia admoneri concedimus cum Scripturâ sacrâ. Et monemus; Semper verbum revelatum esse spectandum : à qvo si qvod somnium nos abducit est, diabolicum, ad quod si nos adducit, est divinum.

II. Qværitur: An sicut in veteri & initio N. T. Angelorum alloqvium hodiè sit expectandum & jactandum? Faciunt hoc nonnulli Fanatici. Nos respondemus 1. Licet DEo nullum revelationis modum possimus præscribere, novimus tamen ex (a) Scriptura : Varium revelationis modum cessasse post Canonem N. T. completum. Unde 2. ad solam Scripturam adstringimur, Luc. 16. v. 29. Joh. 5. v. 39. qvæ propter salutem nostram scripta: Joh. 20. v. 31. Rom. 15. v. 4. & qvidem perfectè, qvia perfectos potest reddere homines, 2. Tim. 3. v. 16. 17. Et 3. disertis verbis extraordinaria spirituum missio negatur hominibus, Luc. 16. v. 31. Qvia 4. res hæc cum maximo incommodo est conjuncta: potest se Satanus transfigurare in Angelum lucis, 2. Cor. 11. v. 14. & actu ipso transfigurat, cùm revelationes diabolicas pro divinis venditat; qvod qvoties factum fuerit, testantur lugenda Papistica, vitæ patrum & experientia qvotidiana.

V. II. Persona mandatum accipiens: Josepus ex Davidica stirpe oriundus: Hujus innuitur 1. Fides, & 2. Promptitudo. Non diu dubitabat nec dormitabat, sed Angelico mandato assentiens piam maturebat fugam; id quod claret 1. Ex assumptione: 2. Ex assumptionis tempore, quæ eâdem, quâ mandatum accepit, peracta est nocte.

VI. III. Persona fuga evadens: Puer is est recens natus; svavis ille Immanuel. Fugit Dominus ille, à cujus conspectu (a) fugit terra: cujus minis (b) tumultuantur aquæ & (c) mare. Puerum (d) nominat Scriptura Christum, ut agnoscamus eum, de quo dictum est: PUER natus est nobis. Non autem solus fugæ datur tenellus & divinus puer, sed adjungitur pater nutritius, & mater virgo: quæ mater non uxor appellatur, quia (e) absoluto partu etiam explosa suspicio est.

VII. Quærit hîc ratio humana: Quare Deus Filium suum fugere voluerit ab illis hostibus, quos fugare potuisset modis innumeris? Cui resp. 1. Considerandum esse in hoc facto divinæ dispensationis Mysterium, & humile Christi ministerium. 2. Dei auxiliandi modum, qui, ubi ordinarium salutis restat medium, extraordinàrium non arripit. 3. Christi imperium seu regnum, quod de hoc mundo non esse sanctâ ostenderat fugâ. Hæc de personis.

VIII. Altera περιστάσεων classis continet circumstantias 1. Temporis, quo fuga suscepta. 2. Loci, ubi peracta. 3. Causarum, propter quas fuga arrepta.

IX. Tempus fugæ Christi vel est inchoationis, vel durationis. Et inchoationis vel remotum vel propinquum. Remotum tempus licet in Scriptura expressè non nominetur, haud obscurè tamen ex circumstantiis non nullis colligitur. (a) Epiphanius putat in secundum à nativitate Christi annum fugam esse rejiciendam, quem sequitur (b) Tostatus Episc. Abul. & (c) Piscator Herbornensis. Sed nobis rectiùs sentire videntur, qui paucas septimanas inter nativitatem & fugam Christi intercessisse existimant. Nam 1. certum est τῷ Χριστῷ γεννηθέντι, mox atque natus est Christus Magos advenisse, Matth. 2. v. 1. 2. Certum est αὐτῶν ἀναχωρησάντων Magis digressis, Angelum apparuisse, v. 13. undé igitur isti bienium compilabunt?

X. Neq; tamen statuimus, eâdem nocte post Magorum discessum Angelum apparuisse, sed omninò inserferenda est historia purificationis juxta legem peractæ, Luc. 2. v. 22. 39. quâ finitâ Angelus Domini apparuit, & fugam mandavit.

XI. Propinqvum tempus dicitur Nox. Sunt qvi multos dies inter Angeli præceptum & Josephi obseqvium intervenisse arbitrantur: Anshelmus, Euthymius, (d) Tostatus, (e) Salmeron, (f) Piscator Herbornensis. Sed nos textui inhærentes rectiùs statuimus: Josephum eadem nocte, quâ mandatum accepit divinum, puerum cum matre assumsisse & in Ægyptum fugisse. 1. Testatur hoc litera expressa. 2. Urgebat id præsens periculum. Nam ut ante Magorum adventum Christi nativitatem cives Hierosolymitani planè ignorabant; ita ante purificationis diem nihil certi speciebat deChristo,in individuo,qvi modò ex confessione Simeonis & Annæ Prophetissæ, Luc. 2. v. 27. seq. innotuerat, ipsi etiam Herodi, qvi inde colligebat, se delusum esse à Magis, unde necem puero intentabat. Opus igitur fuit Josephum eâdem nocte fugere, si Herodis furorem effugere cogitabat. Hanc nostram sententiam amplecti videntur (a) Maldonatus, (b) Barradius & alii.

XII. Durationis tempus indefinitum his exprimitur verbis, ἴσθι ἐκεῖ ἕως ἂν εἴπω σοί. & v. 15. καὶ ἦν ἕως τῆς τελευτῆς Ἡρώδε: posteriora hæc verba priora qvidem determinant, non tamen indicant tempus certum. Infinitum temp⁹ qvi ad definitum cogere laborant, non unius sunt sententiæ. Sunt qvi septem definiunt annos, ut autor Historiæ scholasticæ; & qvi eum seqvuntur: Sunt qvi tres ponunt annos, ut (c) Nicephorus: Veritas unum videtur determinare annum, & si qvid annum excedit. Nam,Qvo anno Herodes Ascalonita fuit defunctus, eo anno Josephus cum suis ex Ægypto fuit revocatus;ut constat ex Angeli promissione: At Herodes defunctus est A.M. 3949. circa Pascha. Ergo. Christus autem in Ægyptum fugerat A.M. 3948. notante Clarissimo Chronologo, Setho Calvisio, p. 463. suæ Isagôges.

XIII. Ex dictis in th. 11. colligi potest circumstantia Loci. In loco considerandus 1. terminus à quo. 2. terminus per quem. 3. terminus ad quem.

XIV. In definiendo termino à quo,autores multum variant. Qvidam constituunt Nazareth, ut Theophylact. & Anshelmus in h. l. ut & (a) Piscator Herbornensis: alii Bethlehem, ut (b) Epiphanius, (c) B. Hunnius, (d) Flaccius: alii Hierosolymam, (e) Centuriæ Magdeb. alii indeterminatum locum intermedium inter Hierosolymam & Nazaretham, ut Palbartus in Pomerio. Primam sententiam nos non defendimus, reliqvas qvas tres ex dictis in th. 10. & 11. conciliari posse existimamus. Non enim errant, qvi Josephum post purificationis actum vel Hierosolymis, vel in Bethlehem, vel in loco aliqvo intermedio vicino pernoctasse, & angelicum mandatum accepisse arbitrantur.

XV. Terminus per quem à plerisque statuitur desertum illud, per qvod filii Israël Palæstinam sunt ingressi. Refert (f) Ludolphus de Saxonia: Christum in deserto ab illo latrone fuisse comprehensum, qvi tempore passionis ab ejus dextris fuerit suspensus. Sed fabulæ qvàm historiæ hæc verisimilior videtur narratio, & promissioni Angelicæ de salvo in Ægyptum adventu non parùm contraria.

XVI. Terminus ad quem est Egyptus, & notatur v. 13. ubi observandus locus tum generalis, (Ægyptus) in textu expressus, cùm specialis, (a) Hermopolis vel Heliopolis ab autoribus appellatus. Qvæstio hîc oritur: An Christus in Ægypto fecerit miracula? Affirmant id (b) Sozomenus, Nicephorus, & ex his (c) Barradius, & (d) Baronius. Nos putamus miracula illa esse figmenta otiosorum hominum, qvæ repugnant dicto Evangelistæ Johannis c. 2. v. 11 2. Puriori (e) antiqvitati: & adversariis sanioribus, pro qvibus respondet (f) Maldonatus, qvi miracula illa fabulis Mahumetanis annumerat.

XVII. Seqvitur circumstantia causarum: qvæ vel principales, & in textu notatæ, vel minùs principales, & à piis doctoribus excogitatæ.

XVIII. Principales causæ fugæ Christi sunt duæ. 1. Herodis malignum studium: μέλλει Ἡρώδης ζητεῖν τὸ παιδίον, τῦ ἀπολέσαι αὐτό. Viderat & præviderat DEUS omniscius malignum Herodis animum, & actionem, qvam meditabatur, tyrannicam, ideò præmonet Josephum ut sine morâ puerum huic malo gliscenti subtrahat. Qværitur hîc: An DEUS cognoscat futura mala contingentia? Negant & pernegant hoc Photiniani, ut videre est in prælectionibus Theolog. Socini c. 8. 9. 10. 11. à pag. 24. usque ad 40. Nos opponimus 1. Præsens exemplum de infanticidio, qvod certè respectu hominum futurum erat, & respectu DEI & hominum malum, imò pessimυm, qvia præcepto divino & charitati proximi summè contrarium. 2. Dicta, qvæ DEUM corda, cogitationes & renes hominum scrutari & cognoscere prædicant Ps. 7. v. 10. Ps. 94. v. 11. 1. Paral. 28. v. 9. & qvidem è longinqvo, Ps. 139. v. 2. id est, cùm nondum actu sunt, v. 4. qvis autem tam absurdus est, ut omnes cogitationes hominum bonas diceret: aut tam impius, ut scripturæ aperte contradiceret, quæ Gen. 6. v. 5. & 8. v. 21. Cogitationes omnes malas pronuntiat. 3. In specie locum, Esa. 41. v. 22. ubi vi antitheseos JEHOVA prædicere dicitur הַבָּאוֹת quæ futura sunt. 4. Quò pertinent omnia illa, quæ partim Christus ipse, partim ejus Apostoli de miseris Ecclesiæ nostri temporis prædixerunt, quibus (proh dolor!) eventus respondet nimis certus.

XIX. Quæritur insuper: An Christianis & in specie doctoribus Ecclesiæ pericula imminentia fugere liceat? Affirmamus licere, si fuga gloriam DEI, salutem proximi & conscientiam propriam non inhibeat vel vulneret. Quod autem quomodo vel fiat vel non fiat, id ex periculo ipso & aliis circumstantiis est judicandum. Affirmationem nostram confirmat Christi consilium, Matth. 10. v. 23. & exemplum Matth. 2. v. 14. Joh. 8. v. 59. Faciant ergo, faciant servi Christi, ministri verbi & Sacramenti ejus, quod præcepit sive permisit, imò quod fecit ipse (videt (a) Augustinus, Hoc enim nobis reliquit exemplum, ut fugiente Domino, fugere indignum non putet servus, inquit (b) Chrysologus. Taceo jus naturæ, quòd homines se periculis subtrahere jubet, licet de auxilio divino non sint incerti: quamdiu enim media ordinaria supersunt, extraordinaria non sunt expectanda: Non enim tentabis Dominum DEUM tuum. Taceo exempla alia tùm Apostolorum, Pauli Act. 9. v. 30. Petri Act. 12. v. 17. cùm Ecclesiæ doctorum, (c) Policarpi, (d) Athanasii, (e) Chrysostomi, qui omnes Christi exemplo se purgarunt.

XX. Secunda causa principalis est Propheticum vaticinium: ideo fugit & revocatus est ex Ægypto, ut impleretur quod dictum erat per Prophetiam: Ex Ægypto vocavi filium meum.

XXI. Duo hîc quæri possunt. 1. An prædictiones rerum inferant necessitatem? Affirmant hoc Stoici Calviniani. (f) Beza dicit: DEUM nihil scire futurum, quod non decreverit futurum. (g) Hyperius ait: quoad DEUM absolutâ necessitate fieri omnia: & Bucanus: Quæ homines vel Angeli agunt, necessario agunt, quoniam DEUS hoc fieri suâ providentiâ decrevit. Nos negamus hoc simpliciter. Concedimus eqvidem DEUM omniu rerum non tantùm τὸ ὅτι prævidere, sed etiam τὸ δι' ὃ & τὸ πῶς; non tamen exinde concludendum, DEUM τοῦ δι' ὃ esse causam. Quod alibi explicatur latiùs. Breviter ita dicimus: Actiones sunt Triplices: Alix divinæ; aliæ humanæ; aliæ diabolicæ. Illæ prædicantur, quia Deus illas certò est operaturus; sic prædicta est resurrectio mortuorum: istæ & hæ prænunciantur, qvia Deus ex certis causis eas eventuras prævidet: sio prædicta est proditio Judæ, &c. Et tamen in nullo actionum genere prædictio est causa. Pulchrè (a) Hieronymus: Non quia Deus futura cognoscit, necesse est, nos facere, quod ille præscivit, sed quod nos propria voluntate sumus facturi, ille novit futurum, quia Deus.

XXII. Qværitur 2. Qvomodo hoc vaticinium propheticum in eductione Christi ex Ægypto dicatur impletum, cùm propriè agere videatur de eductione Israëlitarum? Resp. Scriptura dicitur qvatuor modis impleri, notante Clarissimo Chemnitio c. 12. Harmon. Evang. 1. πρώτως, qvando vaticinio eventus respondet. 2. ἀναλόγως, cùm per similitudinem circumstantiarum vaticinium unum ad plures ac res accommodatur actus. 3. γενικῶς cùm Scriptura oraculum eloqvitur, qvod ad res plures applicari potest. 4. τυπικῶς, cùm aliqvid per rationem typi ad aliud commodatur. Primo modo hoc vaticinium impletum esse statuunt (a) Junius & (b) Piscator Herbornensis: sed qvartus plerisqve arridet Orthodoxis: qvi dicunt, Matthæum ad caput & sponsum Ecclesiæ referre, quod Oseas de corpore & sponsa dixerat, propter arctissimam capitis & corporis mystici conjunctionem: & propter typum, qvem populus Israëliticus gessit in Ægypto.

XXIII. Causæ fugæ in Ægyptum minùs principales, & à doctoribus piis excogitatæ sunt, 1. ut demonstraret se hominem esse nobis per omnia similem. 2. ut nos tyrannorum furorem fugere doceret. 3. ut regni sui modum non mundanum aperiret. 4. ut fugas nostras consecraret.

XXIV. Atqve hæc tibi meditanda in fugâ Christi, anima fugitiva, ne desperes: hæc consideranda, ut lubens & piè fugere discas. Qvod enim Servator fugit, tui fugit causâ, ut fugâ suâ repararet, qvod tu fugâ perdidisti; ut fugâ suâ pararet, qvô tu fugiens es servanda. Ex Paradŷso fugisti in mundi desertum per in obedientiam impiam: Ecce! Christus fugit in Ægytum per promptā obœdientiam; ut hâc sua tuam illam corrigeret. Fugiendum tibi, in hoc erroneo mundo, & patria deserenda dulcis Præsenti sis animo, & caput tuum fugit, ergò

& tu fugies membrum. Reliqvit ille patriam, & in terra remansit profanâ, ut quamvis tibi terram sanctificaret patriam: mansit ibi usq; ad divinum nutú: Et tu in exiliis permane; donec dixerit tibi. Erit, ut lætissimum audias nuntium: Defuncti sunt, qvi quærebant animam tuam. Fugiendum tibi deniq; ex hoc impiò mundo; cùm mortalitatem deponis, & corpus sqvalidæ mandandum terræ: sed nec hîc est qvod metuas. Fugit ille tuus Jesus prior in terram mortis, ex qvâ reversus: ergò & tuum revertetur corpus. Maneat ibi, donec dixerit Dominus: Veniet, veniet Dominus cum voce Archangeli, qvi te ex terrâ revocabit, & læti cantabimus: Absorpens est mors in victoriam!


## 30 Thirtieth Disputation, On the Education and Life of Christ, from the fifth year of his age up to the thirtieth

Whoever looks deeply into the annals of the holy Evangelists, and searches them more profoundly, as they were written by the four amanuenses and secretaries of the Holy Spirit, Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, he will altogether discover that they treat of no one else than JESUS Christ, the Son of God and man, the supreme Prophet, Priest, and King exhibited in the flesh, his words, deeds, passion, and death, etc. Which matter, because it is not only pleasant for the minds of the pious to consider, but also highly useful and necessary to know, we therefore judge that it was done by the command of God. The Bishop of Hippo, St. Augustine, is witness: Whatever he wished the Church to read concerning his words and deeds for all posterity, this he commanded the four Evangelists to write, as if by his own hands, the Head dictating to the members. But they speak chiefly of four things: either of the person of Christ, or his doctrine, or his various and manifold miracles, or of his whole course of life from the time of his birth up to his ascension into heaven. The person of Christ has been sufficiently treated in the preceding disputations: now we are engaged with his life, where in the evangelical history very few things are found besides his birth, which the Evangelists have passed over in deep silence with set purpose, so that we might not be occupied in scrupulously investigating them; but that we might embrace the most principal things with our whole heart and let us devote all our study to weighing them. We have arrived, however, at the education and life of Christ from the fifth year of his age up to the thirtieth, concerning which we have decided to say something on this occasion. But that we may be carried along a certain course, my mind is inclined to reduce this treatise to three heads: of which 1. Is Education 2. Deeds, both specifically and generally. 3. Practical meditation. May Christ Jesus look favorably upon this labor also, undertaken for the glory of His Name, and inspire it from on high!

Thesis I.

Two things are required in every true and pious instruction of children. 1. Bringing them to GOD. 2. Information and education in honesty. Both are found in the parents of Christ.

II. 1. Bringing to the temple. Luke says in c. 2. v. 41. His parents went κατ' ἔτος &c. Where 1. occurs the Departure, the efficient cause of which was the law and command of GOD, by which God in the O.T. demanded that heads of families and males from all of Judea should solemnly visit and religiously observe those three highest and most august feasts at Jerusalem, namely 1. The Feast of the Passover (of Unleavened Bread) 2. The Feast of Weeks (of Firstfruits) and 3. The Feast of Tabernacles (of Booths). 2. The Iteration of the departure, which they did devoutly every year.

III. Although the law primarily obligated males, because the man, who was the head, seemed to make profession for the woman, says Maldonatus: nevertheless, the visitation of the feasts was not forbidden to pious and devout women, provided it was instituted for the sake of religion, and divine worship was performed with pious devotion of mind.

IV. Mary therefore, although she was not compelled by law and lived far from the temple, nevertheless used to come with Joseph her spouse every year to the feast of the Passover to Jerusalem from the city of Nazareth (which, as Barradius says, is distant by a space of 27 leagues).

V. 3. The final cause, specifically, that they might recall the memory of the admirable benefit of the leading out from Egypt, (a) and what was prefigured by that, namely the offering of that immaculate lamb for the sins of the whole world on the altar of the cross (b).

VI. At other times they gathered in general for four main reasons: 1. To perform divine worship by praying. 2. By sacrificing. 3. By hearing the Word, and 4. To give thanks publicly for past benefits.

VII. The Papists attempt to draw this journey of the parents of Christ as an example for their own pilgrimages to various places of the Saints—Rome, Compostela, to Mary of Loreto, etc.—which they undertake for the sake of religion, as can be seen, among others, in Bartsch and Bellarmine, who pursues this at length with both sayings and arguments, at least to defend the Tridentine Conventicle, Session 25.

VIII. But 1. they argue from it ignorantly: because those things commanded by God in the Old Testament, as we saw in thesis 2, were abolished in the New Testament, since they are contrary to the express word of God, and no example of them is read. 2. They undertake them for a different and other end than Mary did, or they do so superstitiously, or to expiate their own or others' sins. 3. Papist pilgrimages are will-worship (ἐθελοθρησκείαι). 4. They are destitute of Orthodox antiquity, as is evident from the Oration of Gregory of Nyssa. See, if you wish, the Examination of Chemnitz.

IX. Of the same flour also is what they urge: that works done from one's own intention of zeal are pleasing to God. Costerus, (a) Bartsch (b), and others teach the very same thing.

X. But they are able to elicit nothing from that. 1. Because it is not permitted to argue from the free action of Mary to meritorious Papist worship. 2. By no means are all works, done with any intention and impulse of the mind, and having the appearance of good, truly good works, but only those which are commanded by God. (c) And Paul condemns such will-worship (ἐθελοθρησκείας) (d). 3. The word of God alone is the norm of good works. (e) 4. The examples of the saints do not make a general rule. 5. Mary went up either because of conjugal love toward Joseph, or because of special gratitude, or because of the knowledge of her Son, or because of some other secret instinct of the Holy Spirit. These things are not in the Papist opinion; therefore, they are entirely irrelevant.

XI. But there is not yet enough of the depravations: they also wish to conclude this from it; that the feasts of Christians are to be celebrated with strict observance: which we concede, if the discussion is about true ones in the Orthodox Church.

XII. We do not, however, for that reason act either with the multitude of holidays in the Papacy destined for the worship of the saints (Bellarmine): or with the Calvinists, who have eliminated the festivals of the holy Apostles: nor with the rigorous, like Danaeus and others, whose fellow-voters were the ancient heretics, the Petrobusians, who abolished all feasts, as is evident from the Life of Bernard: much less with the Mennonites, nor with the Puritans; of whom the former are said to have disturbed the whole order observed from the most ancient times; the latter, however, to have retained only the Lord's days.

XIII. II. Instruction and education for decency, as much in diet as in labor. St. Luke, v. 40, describes this with one single and indeed common word, saying τὸ παιδίον ἤυξανε. Which is well to be noted, since it is the custom of the Evangelists to describe things common to other men either in few words or to pass over them in silence; but to annotate extraordinary things diligently.

XIV. This word is taken from the nutrition and augmentation of the body in children, as Chemnitius notes. Because, therefore, St. Luke uses a common word, it follows that he was educated just like any other infant, so that in his education, just as in the rest of his life, he might be similar, according to St. Paul.

XV. Parents owe two things to their children. 1. Nutrition. Thus Christ also was nourished and sucked the breasts of his mother, as is gathered from Luke 11, 27, and was foretold by the Prophet Isaiah, chap. 7, 15.

XVI. 2. Instruction. A twofold [method] was customary among the people of GOD. The former was general, by which all were instructed at home. The latter was special, by which some were handed over to be educated by teachers in the Synagogues (the Rabbis count over 400), who were called sons of the Prophets. (a) In the latter way he was not instructed, which the Jews testify.

XVII. These holy parents instruct Christ, 1. In piety, which he did not lack, since ἐκραταιἳτο πνέυματι πληρὐμενον σοφίας, just as the divinity and wisdom exerted themselves in him more and more, so that men admired him, as the following history provides us with proof of that matter. 2. In humanity, since having returned home they employed their little son in family affairs.

XVIII. Therefore, the parents of Christ provide an example to all, that they should piously and truly educate and nourish their children out of the natural στοργῇ, which GOD has implanted in the souls of parents.

XIX. Most gravely, therefore, do those sin who entrust their children in their very first infancy to the education and instruction of the Jesuits, sparing either labors or private expenses. For 1. They provide an occasion for idolatry to tender minds. 2. They supply a safeguard for seduction. 3. They intercept the free confession of the truth. Whence re-

And Augustine: The use of the disciplines outside of GOD is most unhappy. All of which things are so great that they ought to make anyone recoil! See the Reminder of Lord Dr. Mylius in the Counsels of Dr. Bidenbach.

XX. Not unlike these were the Jews in the Old Testament, who sacrificed their children to the idol Moloch, which the impious kings Ahaz and Manasseh did.

XXI. 2. Those who utterly neglect all care of their children, whom the Apostle Paul writes are worse than the Heathen (of whom it is read that they exposed their infants in the woods) and have denied the faith. 3. Those who nourish them sumptuously. While they care for the body, they meanwhile neglect the soul. These are like those, says Plutarch, who take care of their shoes, and meanwhile neglect the foot.

XXII. The effect of this education of Christ follows in v. 52, προέκοπτε σοφίᾳ, etc. Which words are said of Christ and can be understood with respect to wisdom either finite, which grew in reality and habitually: or infinite, which grew by external manifestation (or as it seems to some, is understood only of the second act) and effectively, just as the brightness of the Sun is said to grow at midday.

XXIII. The Scholastics, Papists, and Calvinists deny a real increase in the man Christ. Lombard (a), Bellarmine (b), Gregory of Valencia (c), Beza (d), Zanchius (e), Sohnius (f).

XXIV. We first urge the text, which clearly teaches that Christ truly grew in wisdom. 2. From the twofold repetition the same thing is proved, v. 40 and the last, where He is said to have grown both before men and GOD. 3. Luke describes His childhood: whatever the increase was, not in appearance (κατὰ δόκησιν), but truly and really, such also was that of wisdom and grace. 4. Isaiah also testifies that this child did not always know how to refuse the evil. 5. I add the authority of Athanasius and Blessed Luther.

Latin:

QVi annales S. Evangelistarum penitùs introspicit, altiusqve rimatur, prout à qvattuor Spiritus sancti Amanuensibus & Secretariis, Mattheo, Marco, Lucâ & Johanne, sunt conscripti, is omninò deprehendet de nullo alio, qvàm de JESU Christo DEI & hominis Filio, summo Propheta, Sacerdote & Rege in carne exhibito, ejus dictis, factis, passione & morte &c. agere. Qvę res qvia piorũ animis consideratu non modò jucunda, sed & cognitu apprime utilis & necessaria, idcò ex DEI jussu factum esse arbitramur. Testis est Hipponensis Episcopus D. Augustinus: Qvicqvid ille de suis dictis & factis Ecclęsiam ad omnem posteritatem legere voluit, hoc scribendum qvatuor Evangelistis, tanqvam suis manibus, capite membris dictante, imperavit. De qvatuor autem potissimùm, vel de persona Christi, vel doctrinâ, vel de variis & multiplicibus miraculis, vel de toto à nativitatis tempore usq; ad ascensionem in cœlum, vitæ cursu ajunt. De persona Christi sufficienter in superioribus disputationibus actum: jam in vitâ ejus versamur, ubi in historiâ Evangelicâ alias præter nativitatem perpaucâ inveniuntur, qvæ datâ operâ Evangelistæ alto silentio prætererunt, ne in illis scrupulosè investigandis occupemur; sed principalissima toto pectore amplectamur, inqve iis perpendendis omne studium collocemus. Pervenimus autem ad educationem & vitam Christi ab anno ætatis qvinto usqve ad trigesimum, de qvibus hâc vice aliqvid dicere constituimus. Ut autem certo feramur cursu, ad tria capita hanc πραγματείαν revocare fert animus: qvorum 1. Est Educatio 2. Res gestæ, tum in specie tum in genere. 3. Meditatio practica. Christus Jesus huic qvoq; labori in Nominis sui gloriam suscepto benè faveat & adspiret ex alto!

Thesis I.

DUo in omni verâ & piâ liberorum institutione reqviruntur. Ad DEUM adductio. 2. Ad honestatem informatio & educatio. Utrumq; reperitur in parentibus Christi.

II. 1. Ad templum adductio. Lucas ait c. 2. v. 41. Ibant parentes ejus κατ' ἔτος &c. Ubi 1. occurrit Profectio, cujus causa efficiens fuit lex & mandatum DEI, qvo Deus in V. T. postulabat, ut patresfamilias & masculi ex universâ Judæâ tria illa festa summa & augustissima Hierosolymis solenniter visitent & religiosè observent, nempe 1. Festum Paschatos (Azymorum) 2. Festum hebdomatum (Primitiarum) & 3. Festum tabernaculorum (Scenopegiorum). 2. Iteratio profectionis, id qvod devote qvotannis façiebant.

III. Etsi verò lex imprimis masculos obligebat, qvia vir, qvi caput erat, pro fœminâ profiteri videbatur, ait Maldonatus: tamen piis & devotis mulieribus visitatio festorum non fuit prohibita, modò id religionis causâ instituebatur, cultusq; divinus piâ animi devotione peragebatur.

IV. Maria itaqve, etsi non cogebatur lege & longè à templo habitabat, tamen cum Josepho sponso suo qvotannis ad festum Paschatos Hierosolymam in civitatem Nazareth (qvæ, ut Barradius ait, 27. Leucarum spatio distat) venire solebat.

V. 3. Causa finalis, in specie, ut memoriam revocarent admirandum eductionis ex Ægypto beneficium, (a) & qvod per istud præfiguratum est, nempe agni illius immaculati pro totius mundi peccatis in arâ crucis oblatio (b).

VI. Aliàs in genere qvattuor potissimùm de causis convenerunt. 1. Ut cultum divinum orando. 2. Sacrificando. 3. Verbum audiendo perficerent, & 4. Publicè pro beneficiis præteritis gratias agerent.

VII. Hanc profectionem parentum Christi in exemplum suarum peregrinationum, ad varia Sanctorum loca, Roman', Compostellas, ad Mariam Lauretanam &c. trahere conantur Pontificii, qvas religionis causâ suscipiunt, ut præter alios videre est apud Bartscium & Bellarminum, qvi & dictis & rationibus fusè perseqvitur, saltem ut Tridentini Conciliabuli Sess. 25. defendat.

VIII. Verùm 1. ἀπαιδεύτως inde argumentantur: qvia in V. T. à Deo mandatæ, uti th. 2. vidimus, in N. T. sublatæ sunt, siqvidem contra expressum Dei verbum sunt, neq; exemplum legitur. 2. Alio & diverso fine qvàm Maria, vel superstitiose suscipiunt, vel ut sua vel aliorum peccata expiant. 3. Peregrinationes Pontificiæ ἐθελοθρησκείαι sunt. 4. Destituuntur Orthodoxâ antiqvitate, ut ex Orat. Greg. Nysseni patet. Vide si libet Examen Chemnitii.

IX. Ejusdem qvoq; farinæ est, qvod urgent: Opera ex propriâ zeli intentione facta, Deo grata esse. Docet idipsum Costerus, (a) Bartscius (b) & alii.

X. Ast nihil inde elicere valent. 1. Qvia à liberâ actione Mariæ ad cultus Papisticos meritorios argumentari non licet. 2. Neqvaqvam qvævis opera, qvovis intento, & animi impulsu facta, & specimen boni habentia, verè sunt bona opera, sed illa tantùm, qvæ sunt mandata à Deo. (c) Et Paulus hujusmodi ἐθελοθρησκείας (d) damnat. 3. Verbum Dei solùm est norma bonorum operum. (e) 4. Exempla sanctorum non faciunt regulam generalem. 5. Maria ascendit vel ob amorem conjugalem erga Josephum, vel ob specialem gratitudinem, vel ob Filii cognitionem, vel ob alium arcanum Spiritus S. instinctum. Hæc in Pontificiâ sententiâ non sunt; prorsus ergo aliena sunt.

XI. Verùm nondum satis est depravationum: etiam hoc inde concludere volunt; Festa Christianorum strictâ observatione celebranda: qvod concedimus, si de veris in Ecclesiâ Orthodoxâ sermo est.

XII. Non tamen ideò facimus vel cum multitudine feriarum in Papatu divorum cultui destinatarum (Bellarminus): vel cum Calvinianis, qvi Sanct. Apostolorum festivitates eliminarunt: neqve cum rigorosis, ut Danæus & alii, qvorum ὁμόψηφοι Petrobusiani veteres hæretici, omnia festa tollentes, ut ex Vitâ Bernhardi liqvet: multò minùs cum Mennonistis, neqve cum Puritanis; quorum illi omnem ordinem ab antiqvissimis temporibus observatum turbasse; hi verò solas Dominicas retinuisse perhibentur.

XIII. II. Ad honestatem informatio & educatio tam in victu qvàm in labore. D. Lucas v. 40. unico tantùm & qvidem vulgari verbo describit, inqviens τὸ παιδίον ἤυξανε. Qvod probè notandum, siqvidem Evangelistarum mos est, communia cum cæteris hominibus, vel paucis describere, vel silentio præterire; extraordinaria verò diligenter annotare.

XIV. Sumitur verbum hoc de nutritione & augmentatione corporis in pueris, annotante Chemnitio. Qvia ergò D. Lucas communi utitur verbo, seqvitur, qvòd educatus fuerit sicut alius quispiam infans, ut & in educatione, qvemadmodum in reliqvâ vitâ, esset similis, juxta Divum Paulum.

XV. Duo autem suis liberis debent parentes. 1. Nutritionem. Sic Christus qvoq; nutritus fuit & ubera matris suxit, ut colligitur ex Luc. 11, 27. & prædictum fuit à Prophetâ Esaiâ, cap. 7, 15.

XVI. 2. Institutionem. Duplex in populo DEI erat usitata. Prior generalis, qvâ omnes domi informabantur. Posterior specialis, qvâ nonnullis præceptoribus inSynagogis (Rabbini numerant ultra 400) erudiendi tradebantur, qvi Prophetarum filii dicti. (a) Posteriori modo hoc non fuit institutus, id qvod testantur Judæi.

XVII. Hi sancti parentes Christum instituunt, 1. Inpietate, qvâ non egebat, siqvidem ἐκραταιἳτο πνέυματι πληρὐμενον σοφίας, prout sese divinitas & sapientia in ex magis exeruit, ita ut ipsum homines admirarentur, sicut nobis seqvens historia ejus rei documentum præbet. 2. Inhumanitate, siqvidem domum reversi filiolum suum ad rem familiarem adhibuerunt.

XVIII. Exemplum igitur præbent parentes Christi omnibus, ut liberos suos ex στοργῇ naturali, quam DEUS implantavit animis parentum, piè & verè educant & enutriant.

XIX. Gravissimò ergò peccant ii, qvi liberos suos in prima statim infantia Jesuvitarum educationi & institutioni concredunt, parcentes vel laboribus, vel sumptibus privatis. Nam 1. Occasionem præbent idololatriæ teneris mentibus. 2. Præsidium seductionis subministrant. 3. Intercipiunt liberam veritatis confessionem. Unde re-

Etè Augustinus: Disciplinarum usus extra DEUM, maximè infelix est. Quæ omnia tanta sunt, ut quemvis abhorrere debeat! Videatur Commonefactio Dn. D. Mylii in Consiliis D. Bidenbachii.

XX. Quibus non absimiles fuerunt Judæi in Veteri Testamento, qui liberos suos sacrificarunt idolo Moloch, quod fecerunt impii reges Achatz & Manasse.

XXI. 2. Qui prorsus negligunt omnem liberorum suorum curam, quod D. Apostolus Paulus Ethnicis, (de quibus legitur, infantes suos exposuisse in sylvis) deteriores esse & fidem abnegasse scribit. 3. Qui sumptuose alunt. Dum corpus curant, interim negligunt animum. Hi similes sunt iis, ait Plutarchus, qui calceorum curam habent, & interim pedem negligunt.

XXII. Hanc educationem Christi sequitur effectus v. 52. παρέκοπτε σοφίᾳ, &c. Quæ verba de Christo dicuntur & intelligi possunt respectu sapientiæ vel finitæ, quæ crevit reipsa & habitualiter: vel infinitæ, quæ crevit externâ manifestatione (vel ut quibusdam videtur, de actu tantùm secundo intelligitur) & effectualiter, ut Solis claritas crescere dicitur in meridie.

XXIII. Scholastici, Pontificii, & Calviniani reale incrementum in homine Christo negant. Lombardus (a) Bellarminus, (b) Gregorius de Valentia, (c) Beza, (d) Zanchius, (e) Sohnius. (f)

XXIV. Nos primò urgemus τὸ ῥητὸν, quod perspicuè docet Christum reverâ crevisse sapientia. 2. Ex bina repetione probatur id ipsum, v. 40. & ult. ubi & apud homines & DEUM crevisse dicitur. 3. Lucas pueritiam describit: quale ergo fuit incrementum, non κατὰ δόκησιν, sed verè & realiter, tale etiam erat sapientiæ & gratiæ. 4. Esaias quoq; testatur, non semper puerum hunc scivisse reprobare malum. 5. Addo autoritatem Athanasii & B. Lutheri.


### XXV. But how did Christ progress according to His human nature, when…

XXV. But how did Christ progress according to His human nature, when nevertheless He was full of infinite wisdom, Col. 2:9, immediately from conception? To that I say that one must distinguish between omniscience and its use, or between possession (κτῆσιν) and use (χρῆσιν). 2. Between the state of exaltation and humiliation. 3. In the human mind of Christ from the moment of conception all the treasures of divine knowledge and wisdom were hidden, but He abstained from the use of that wisdom voluntarily and by divine economy (οἰκονομίαν) in the state of humiliation. 4. The Bethlehemite boy, who grew in wisdom as a man, according to the proper knowledge of his mind was nevertheless πληρούμενος [being filled] with the proper wisdom of the Son of GOD, v. 40, regarding the first act of the personal union. But enough about his education.

XXVI. Now something must be said concerning the deeds done, which are considered either εἰδικῶς [specifically] or γενικῶς [generally].

XXVII. Εἰδικῶς [Specifically] 1. It was a singular thing that he disputed with astonishment in the midst of the Doctors, v. 46, 47. It is commonly said that those endowed with heroic talents cannot remain hidden, but soon from the years of childhood do something. We have an example in our Savior, who, having scarcely progressed from the threshold of childhood, made his divine nature and wisdom manifest.

XXVIII. And immediately is indicated 1. The place, where the disputation took place: the Evangelists say in the temple; Dr. Chemnitz observed [it was] around the temple, because other buildings also attached to the temple were called the temple.

XXIX. 2. Luke does not explain the subject matter of this disputation, unless one wishes to refer to this: 'I must be about my Father's business': Vincent [speaks] of the seventy years of Daniel, and of the scepter taken away from the tribe of Judah: Others [speak] of the office and advent of the Messiah: which, because they are uncertain, the pious opinion of Blessed Clement pleases us, which see.

XXX. Why, moreover, Christ wished to give a specimen of his wisdom in his twelfth year, Maldonatus gives this reason, because at that time especially the talent of boys begins to appear and to be apt for grasping letters.

XXXI. And that specimen, which the boy Jesus gave there, was divine and altogether excellent, Luke shows v. 46, 47. For it is perceived from this, that from the midst of his emptying, rays of his majesty shone forth most brilliantly. 1. It is the wisdom of Christ, by which with wonderful sagacity of mind he taught in the midst of the doctors, and with the sharpness of disputing he inquired concerning the true use and sound meaning of the Prophets to the astonishment of the doctors. 2. By which he revealed his divinity to his parents, v. 49.

XXXII. By this example the use of Theological disputations and other exercises of that kind are consecrated, which certain Politicians attempt to remove from the midst, as Licinius the tyrant, according to the testimony of Eusebius (a), Bodin, and Durus de Pascolo in the Aulico-Politico.

XXXIII. But we prove the contrary. 1. By the example of Christ, who not only here, but also elsewhere, as in John 9:2, etc., he held a disputation. 2. By the practice of the Apostolic Church. Augustine testifies that in the ancient Church both lectures and disputations concerning sacred matters were held. 3. Necessity requires that we prepare ourselves for the fight, since an account of the faith must be given to everyone who asks, according to St. Peter. 4. The highest utility ought to recall us to this kind of exercise, since in this way minds are polished, judgment is rightly formed, and heretics are more easily refuted and avoided.

XXXIV. Another kind of the deeds of Christ in his youth is peculiar and proper to the Nazarene. For the true Messiah is the נֵצֶר (netzer), a shoot or sprout rising from the root of Jesse. From this name the city of Nazareth was named, and from it Christ was called Nazarenus, who elsewhere is called Ναζαραῖος, likewise ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ.

XXXV. Jerome says this opinion is that of the wise men of the Hebrews, who assert that this name of the Nazarene must be written with צ; which we prove to be more probable in this way.

XXXVI. 1. From the etymology. It is derived from the name נֵצֶר, by which is signified a shoot and a flower sprouting from a cut-down and dead trunk, and as it were growing up from the sap preserved within; and thus Nazareth is as it were the city of the flower or of flowers. Which is derived from נָצַר, which in Latin is, he guarded, he preserved.

XXXVII. 2. From the fulfillment of the predictions by the Prophets. For St. Matthew, ch. 2:23, says that he took the name from the city for this reason, that what was predicted by the prophets might be fulfilled, namely by Isaiah (a) and by Zechariah (b).

XXXVIII. 3. From the truth of the matter. For Christ, as the true נֹצֵר (notzer), is to come forth from that city, who saved, preserved, and conserved the whole human race from the tyranny and power of the Devil. For this is he who in the Canticle professes himself the keeper of the vineyards. And thus far concerning the actions in particular.

XXXIX. Now those things which he did generally come to be explained, which he embraces in the last two verses, verses 51 and 52, in which he leaves as it were an epitome of the life of Christ up to the 30th year of his age, while the others are silent. XL. Where 1. The obedience of Christ is described v. 51. He descended into Nazareth etc. which was the fatherland of Christ by reason of both conception (c) and education, (d) For the Lord dwelt in Nazareth from infancy up to a settled and mature age.

XLI. 2. Subjection and humility, v. 51. καὶ ἦν ὑποτασσόμενος. O admirable thing! God is subject to men, the creator to the creature, the Lord to his own subjects. The word ὑποτασσόμενος, as Chemnitz notes, signifies that external actions are governed by the dominion of another superior: hence the Syrian rendered it עבד serving them.

XLII. This subjection, however, is to be understood with limitations, because it behooves Christ to be in those things which are the Father's, v. 49. Origen, Augustine, Euthymius, and Hugo think that the things which were his Father's are called the temple. But Christ speaks of the will of the Father, in which he consists in executing the office for which he was sent into the world, and having fully undertaken that in the 30th year of his age, he wished here to provide at least a prelude. Now these are: 1. To teach. 2. To intercede for the people. 3. To sacrifice. 4. To bless the people.

XLIII. The practice of the carpenter's trade, from the same verse. Paul of Burgos, the Bishop, St. Augustine, and Simon of Cassia do indeed deny that Christ learned any trade. But the contrary is proven 1. From this passage. 2. From the open testimony of Matthew and Mark, where he is named not so much the son of a carpenter, but the carpenter himself. 3. From the assertion of his fellow-countrymen, Mark 6, who call him τέκτονα. 4. From antiquity. Justin in Trypho, Basil, Cardinal Cajetan on ch. 6 of Mark and part 3, beginning of question 40, Dionysius the Carthusian, Abulensis, and Lyra on ch. 6 of Mark.

XLIV. Christ subjected himself to his parents for this reason, that by this unmerited obedience he might satisfy God the Father for the disobedience of children, and that he might exhort children by his example to obey their parents and to help them as much as they are able. And by his own craft, Christ consecrated all crafts, so that a pious man should not be ashamed of such a kind of life (if circumstances so require).

XLV. Johannes Piscator indeed says that Christ, according to his humanity, owed obedience to his parents, partly as a son of Adam, partly as a son of Israel. But it is 1. Against the express word of God, which testifies everywhere that he owed nothing to anyone of himself according to either nature as the Lord of the law to provide obedience. 2. Because not a mere man, but the God-man was subject to his parents. 3. Because he subjected himself to the law for this reason, that he might redeem us, who were under the law. 4. From the contrary. If he had been a debtor, he could not have merited anything for others by his own obedience. 5. The rule of the Council of Chalcedon pertains here. Each nature does what is proper to itself. And what is commonly said in the Schools: The names of the office belong to Christ, etc. Let the most illustrious Lord D. Menzerus, my preceptor to be honored eternally, be consulted.

XLVI. Concerning the labor of Christ, 1. The Romanists have invented various and many miracles performed by Christ as a boy, such as that he formed flying birds and walking little men from clay, just as they fable in the book concerning the infancy of Christ.

XLVII. But 1. without Scripture, which if it is silent, we also must be silent, since the Holy Spirit has diligently described such deeds elsewhere. Therefore, we leave those most trifling trifles to their authors. 2. The evangelical history clearly testifies that he performed no miracle before he entered upon his public office. For the beginning of his miracles was in Cana of Galilee. John 2:11.

XLVIII. Nor is there any reason for anyone to insist that, by teaching, the first sign was in Cana of Galilee, yet it does not follow from that that he performed none elsewhere. For the Greek text expressly contradicts this to the face, 'Jesus did this beginning of signs,' v. 11. Chrysostom urges this very point. Therefore, let us remain in the opinion of Jerome, to Helvidius: That he gave a specimen of his future office by teaching, we believe, because we read it: concerning miracles before his 30th year, we do not read. Therefore, we neither assert nor believe them.

XLIX. Thomas gives this reason. In the middle time, namely from his birth up to his Baptism, he performed no miracle, but was of a life conformable to others, and his power remained unknown to all. He performed miracles in the middle time for this reason, so that the mystery of the incarnation might not be thought to be a phantom: if he had not behaved himself like other infants in age: and therefore he deferred the demonstration of his knowledge and power to that time in which other men are accustomed to flourish in knowledge and power.

L. II. The Anabaptists gather from this: Christ labored with his hands:

Therefore, ministers of the Church must also labor. For we ought to imitate the example of Christ.

LI. But the Anabaptists indeed use this argument, yet without a command. For 1. although Christ in his infancy helped his father Joseph by laboring, and thus sanctified the labor commanded by God in Gen. 3, 16, nevertheless, after he undertook the ministry of teaching, he laid it aside. Thus he called the Apostles to this end, that they should leave the ship and the nets. (a) 2. Manual labor hinders the works of the calling. But if it pertained to the calling or office of a minister, Christ himself would have used it, and would have commanded his own Apostles to labor at the same time. Therefore, let them be brought forward by the Adversaries without qualification.

LII. Therefore, this meditation ought to make us both pious and humble. Pious, that we may reverently worship GOD, and seek him both at home and abroad, by the example of Mary, who with sorrow sought Christ for three days, and at length found him in the temple. Thus, O pious soul, in a similar manner inquire for Christ and say: Grant me to desire you: by desiring to seek you: by seeking to find you: by finding to love you: by loving to redeem my evils: by having redeemed them, not to repeat them. And you who grant to the one asking: are found by the one seeking: are opened to the one knocking: do not deny me what you promise to all. Humble, by the example of Christ, who took the form of a servant, becoming obedient to the Father. Phil. 2, 7. Blush, proud ash: God humbles himself, and you exalt yourself!

Pray, O faithful soul, in this manner: Repel from me all the pride of arrogance, and all appetites for vain glory: and all things at once, which generate such a plague and such malice in me. Make me to be a little one in your eyes, that I may find full grace in the eyes of your majesty.

Latin:

XXV. Quomodo autem Christus juxta humanam naturam profecerit, cùm tamen plenus fuerit sapientiâ infinitâ, Col. 2, 9. illicò à conceptione? Ad istud dico distinguendum esse inter omniscientiam & ejus usurpationem, seu inter κτῆσιν & χρῆσιν. 2. Inter statum exaltationis & exinanitionis. 3. In humanâ Christi mente à momento conceptionis omnes thesauri scientiæ & sapientiæ divinæ fuerunt absconditi, sed usu ejus sapientiæ spontè & per οἰκονομίαν abstinuit in statu humilitatis. 4. Puellus Bethlehemiticus, qvi crevit sapientiâ ut homo, secundùm propriam mentis scientiam nihilominùs fuit πληρούμενος sapientiâ Filii DEI propriâ, v. 40. qvoad actum primum unionis personalis. Sed satis de educatione.

XXVI. Nunc de rebus gestis aliqvid dicendum, qvæ considerantur vel εἰδικῶς vel γενικῶς.

XXVII. Εἰδικῶς 1. Singulare fuit, qvod cum stupore in medio Doctorum disputarit, v. 46. 47. Dicisolet, Heroicis ingeniis præditos non posse latere, sed mox â pueritiæ annis qvadam agere. Exemplum habemus in Salvatore nostrœ, qvi vix â pueritiæ limine progressus divinam naturam & sapientiam testatam fecit.

XXVIII. Et statim indicatur 1. Locus, ubinam facta sit disputatio: Evangelistæ dicunt in templo; D. Chemnitius observavit circa templum, qvia alia qvoq; ædificia templo adjuncta vocabantur templum.

XXIX. 2. Materiam disputationis hujus Lucas non explicat, nisi qvis huc referre velit illud: In his qvæ Patris mei sunt, oportet me esse: Vincentius de septuaginta annis Danielis, & de sceptro de tribu Judæ ablato: Alii de Messiæ officio & adventu: qvæ qvia incerta sunt, nobis pia B. Clementii sententia placet, qvam vide.

XXX. Cur a. Christus duodecimo anno sapientiæ suæ specimen edere voluerit, Maldonatus hanc rationem dat, qvia eo tempore potissimum incipit puerorum ingenium apparere & capessendis literis aptum esse.

XXXI. Et specimen illud, qvod puer Jesus ibi edidit, fuisse divinum & admodum eximium, Lucas ostendit v. 46. 47. Nam perspicitur inde, qvod ex mediâ exinanitione ejus redii prælustres majestatis suæ exsplenduerint. 1. Est sapientia Christi, qvâ mirâ animi sagacitate in medio doctorum docuit, & disputandi acrimoniâ percontatus est de vero usu & sanâ Prophetarum sententiâ cum stupore doctorum. 2. Qvâ parentibus suam divinitatem patefecit, v. 49.

XXXII. Exemplo hoc consecrantur disputationum Theologicarum usus, aliæq; ejusmodi exercitia, qvos Politici qvidam è medio tollere conantur, ut Licinius tyrannus, teste Eusebio (a), Bodinus & Durus de Pascolo in Aulico-Politico.

XXXIII. Verùm contrarium probamus. 1. Exemplo Christi, qvi non tantùm hîc, sed etiam alibi, ut Joh. 9, 2. &c. disputationem habuit. 2. Praxi Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ. Augustinus testatur in Ecclesiâ veteri & prælectiones & disputationes qvoqve de rebus sacris habitas fuisse. 3, Necessitas reqvirit, ut ad pugnam nos præparemus, cùm cuilibet petenti ratio fidei reddenda, juxta D. Petrum. 4. Utilitas summa nos ad hoc exercitii genus revocare debet, siqvidem hoc modo ingenia expoliuntur, judicium rectè formatur, & hæretici faciliùs refutantur & evitantur.

XXXIV. Alterum genus rerum gestarum Christi in adolescentia peculiare & proprium Nazareno. Est enim Messias verus נֵצֶר furculus seu germen de radice Isai exurgens. Ab hoc nomine Nazareth urbs dicta est, & ab illâ Christus dictus Ναζαρηνὸς, qvi alibi Ναζαραῖος, item ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ.

XXXV. Hanc sententiam dicit Hieronymus esse sapientum Hebræorum, qvi asserunt nomen hoc Nazaræni scribendum esse per צ; qvam probabiliorem esse ita probamus.

XXXVI. 1. Ab Etymologiâ. Derivatur à nomine נֵצֶר, qvo significatur surculus & flos è trunco succiso atqve intermortuo repullulans, & qvasi asservato intus succo subolescens; & ita Nazareth esse qvasicivitas floris seu florum. Qvod derivatur à נָצַר, qvod Latinè est, custodivit, servavit.

XXXVII. 2. A prædictionum per Prophetas impletione. D. Matthæus enim c. 2, 23. ait, ideò nomen ab urbe accepisse, ut impleretur, qvod prædictum est διὰ τῶν προφητῶν, nempè per Esaiam (a) & per Zachariam (b).

XXXVIII. 3. A rei veritate. Christus enim ut verus נֹצֵר ex eâ proditurus est civitate, qvi totum genus humanum servavit, præservavit & conservavit à tyrannide & potestate Diaboli. Hic enim ille est, qvi in Cantico se custodem vinearum profitetur. Atq; hactenus de actionibus in specie.

XXXIX. Jam exponenda veniunt, qvæ γενικῶς egerit, postremis duobus versiculis complectitur, vers. 51, 52. in qvibus veluti epitomen vitæ Christi usqve ad 30. ætatis annum, relinqvis tacentibus. XL. Ubi 1. Obedientia Christi describitur v. 51. Descendit in Nazareth &c. quæ patria Christi ratione & conceptionis (c) & educationis, (d) Habitavit enim Dominus in Nazareth inde ab infantiâ usqve ad statam & maturam ætatem.

XLI. 2. Subjectio & humilitas, v. 51. καὶ ἦν ὑποτασσόμενος. O rem admirandam! Deus hominibus, creator creaturæ, Dominus subditis suisqve suis sit subditus. Vox ὑποτασσόμενος, annotante Chemnitio, significat externas actiones alterius superioris dominio gubernari: hinc Syrus עבד ministrans eis reddidit.

XLII. Limitatè tamen hæc subjectio est intelligenda, quia oportet Christum esse in his, quæ Patris sunt, v. 49. Origenes, Augustinus, Euthymius & Hugo putant ea, quæ patris sui erant, templum appellari. Ast Christus de voluntate Patris loqvitur, quâ in exeqvendo officio, ob qvod missus erat in mundum, consistit, istudqve anno 30. ætatis suæ plenè aggressus, & hic præludium saltem edere voluit. Sunt autem hæc 1. Docere. 2. Pro populo intercedere. 3. Sacrificare. 4. Populo benedicere.

XLIII. Fabrilis artis tractatio, ex eodem versu. Negant qvidem Paulus Burgensis Episcopus D. Augustinus & Simon de Cassia, artem ullam dedicisse Christum. Verùm contrarium probatur 1. Ex hoc loco. 2. Ex aperto testimonio, Matthæi & Marci, ubi non tam fabri filius, sed & faber ipse nominatur. 3. Ex asservatione Sympatriotarum, Marc. 6. qvi τέκτονα vocant. 4. Ex vetustate. Justinus in Typhone, Basilius, Cajetanus Cardinalis in c. 6. Marc. & parte 3. initio qvæst. 40. Dionysius Carthusianus, Abulensis & Lyra in c. 6. Marci.

XLIV. Ideo autem Christus sese subjecit parentibus suis, ut hâc indebitâ obedientiâ pro liberorum inobedientiâ Dei Patri satisfaceret, & ut hortaretur suo exemplo liberos, ut parentibus pareant, eosqve pro virili juvent. Et suo opificio Christus omnia opificia consecravit, ut hominem pium talis generis vitæ (si ita res ferat) pudere non debeat.

XLV. Johannes Piscator qvidem dicit, Christum juxta humanitatem debuisse obedientiam suis parentibus, partim ut filium Adæ, partim ut filium Israëlis. Verùm est 1. Contra expressum Dei verbum, qvod passim testatur per se nemini debuisse secundum utramq; naturam ceu Dominum legis præstare obedientiam. 2. Qvia non ψιλὸς, sed θεάνθρωπος subjectus est parentibus. 3. Qvia ideo se subjecit legi, ut nos redimeret, qvi sub lege eramus. 4. A contrario. Si debitor fuisset, aliis suâ obedientiâ promereri aliqvid non potuisset. 5. Pertinet huc regula Concilii Chalcedonensis. Utraq; agit, qvod sibi proprium. Et qvod in Scholis vulgò dicitur: Nomina officii competunt Christo, &c. Videatur Clariss. Dn. D. Menzerus, Præceptor meus æternum honorandus.

XLVI. Circa laborem Christi, 1. Romanenses varia & multa vixerunt miracula à Christo puero edita, ut qvòd è certâ aves volantes, & virunculos incedentes formarrit, prout in libro de infantiâ Christi fabulantur.

XLVII. Sed 1. ἄτερ γραφῆς, qvæ si tacet & nobis qvoqve tacendum erit, siqvidem Spiritus Sanctus talia facta aliàs diligenter descripsit. Nugas proinde istas nugatissimas suis autoribus relinqvimus. 2. Evangelica historia clarè testatur, nullum, anteqvam officium publicum ingressus, fecisse miraculum. Initium enim miraculorum in Canâ Galileæ fuit. Joh. 2, 11.

XLVIII. Neq; est, ut qvis instet, docendo, primum fuisse signum in Canâ Galileæ, non tamen inde seqvi, qvod alibi nullum fecerit. Nam textus Græcus expressè in os contradicit, ταύτην ἐποίησε τὴν ἀρχὴν τῶν σημείων ὁ Ἰησῦς, v. 11. Urget hoc ipsum Chrysostomus. Qvare maneamus in sententia Hieronymi, ad Helvidium: Qvod specimen futuri sui officii docendo ediderit, credimus, qvia legimus: de miraculis ante annum 30. non legimus. Ergo nec affeveramus nec credimus.

XLIX. Thomas hanc rationem dat. Medio tempore scilicet à nativitate usq; ad Baptismum nullum miraculum operatus est, sed conformis conversationis aliis erat, & sua virtus ignota omnibus existebat. Ideo autem fecit miracula medio tempore, ut non putaretur, mysterium incarnationis esse phantasma: si non se habuisset sicut alii ætate infantes: & ideò demonstrationem scientiæ & virtutis suæ ad id tempus distulit, in qvo alii homines scientiâ & virtute vigere consveverunt.

L. II. Anabaptistæ exinde colligunt: Christus laboravit manibus:

Ergo etiam ministris Ecclesiæ est laborandum. Christi enim exemplum imitari debemus.

LI. Verùm Anabaptistæ hoc qvidem utuntur argumento, fine tamen præcepto. Nam 1. licet Christus infantiâ patrem Josephum adjuvit laborando; & ita laborem Gen. 3, 16. divinitùs mandatum, sanctificavit, tamen postquam ministerium docendi aggressus, deposuit. Sic vocavit Apostolos hunc in finem, ut relinqverent navem & retia. (a) 2. Labor manuarius impedit opera vocationis. Qvod si ad vocationem seu officium ministri pertineret, Christus ipse & usus fuisset, suosqve Apostolos simul jussisset laborare. A' προσδιορίστως ergo ab Adversariis adducantur.

LII. Hæc ergò meditatio & pios & humiles nos facere debet. Pios, ut reverenter colamus DEUM, & qværamus tum domi tum foris, exemplo Mariæ, qvæ cum dolore per triduum qvæsivit Christum, & tandem in templo inventis. Ita, ô anima pia, simili modo inqvire Christum & dic: Da mihi te desiderare: desiderando qværere: qværendo invenire: inveniendo amare: amando mala mea redimere: redemta non iterare. Et qvi petenti largiris: qværenti inveniris: pulsando aperiris: non deneges mihi, qvod omnibus promittis. Humiles, exemplo Christi, qvi formam servi sumsit, obediens factus Patri. Phil. 2, 7. Erubesce superbe cinis: Deus se humiliat, & tu te exaltas!

Ora, ô fidelis anima, hunc in modum: Repelle à me omnes superbiæ fastus, cunctosqve inanis gloriæ appetitus: & omnia simul, qvæ tantam pestem tantamq; malitiam in me generant. Fac ut sim parvulus in oculis tuis, ut plenam gratiam in oculis majestatis tuæ inveniam.


## 31 Thirty-first Disputation, On the Baptism of Christ, and the Beginning of his Ministry

As the priests and Levites in the O. T., about to enter the tabernacle of the Lord, washed their hands before they attended to sacred duties in the atrium: so the true and only Priest of the N. T., Christ Jesus, about to undertake his ministry and the office of redemption having been perfected, willed to be inaugurated into the same through the reception of baptism. The holy quaternion of the Gospels, however, describes the history of the baptism of Christ, concerning which, as the order of the subject requires, with God graciously assisting, we are to examine in the present, in Matth. 3, 13. Marc. 1, 9. Luc. 3, 21. Joh. 1, it only by allusion, seeing without doubt that it had been sufficiently and more than enough set forth in writing by the other Evangelists. But although this history is clearly august and illustrious, the individual circumstances of which are worthy to be considered with due diligence, both because of the beginning of Christ's ministry and also because of the most weighty matters which are contained in it, nevertheless for this time, that we may examine what is most necessary to be known and noted, we shall weigh five chapters, intending to treat 1. of the circumstances of time and place. 2. Of the ministerial cause dispensing the baptism. 3. Of the act of baptism itself and the miracles that followed it. 4. Of the final cause, why Christ received baptism. 5. Of the brief and pious application of this history.

Thesis I.

There are two circumstances, as Chytræus testifies, by which the certainty of historical truth is demonstrated, namely time and place; it would therefore be worth the effort if we also attend to the time and place in this history. But since, regarding the time, as to the day and the month, a wonderful variety of opinions and calculations presents itself, we therefore do not wish to be so curious at present as to presume to note any certain determination of the day and month, being destitute of the guidance and light of Scripture, but content with a simple narration of certain opinions, we shall reveal in a single word to which opinion we are more inclined.

II. Certain postillators (for so Chemnitius speaks) and Papists have not doubted to determine a certain and precise day, asserting that Christ was baptized on the sixth day of January, but 1. without any foundation in Scripture: for neither did the Evangelists expressly note the day, nor can it be gathered certainly, exactly, and precisely from the circumstances of the history. 2. Without any or even a probable reason, relying only on bare conjecture and the uncertain tradition of the ancients.

III. Some, because the Jordan is accustomed to fill all its banks at the time of harvest, as is read in Joshua 3, 15 and Sirach 24, 36, therefore suppose that this baptism happened before the harvest, for at that time the banks had not yet been filled, since for Christ and John to have had to descend into the Jordan is proven by the fact that Jesus, having been baptized, is said to have immediately ascended out of the water.

IV. Others, thinking that John the Baptist began his ministry on the very feast of trumpets, that is, on the first day of the seventh month, maintain that Christ was baptized ten days later on the very feast of atonement, and thus began and celebrated the true feast of propitiation, which was more obscurely foreshadowed by the Mosaic one. From which, indeed, a most elegant analogy between the Old and New Testament can be established, although traces of this calculation are nowhere to be found in the Evangelical history.

V. Dr. Chemnitius deduces the time of the baptism and the beginning of the ministry from probable conjectures to the beginning of December or the end of November, if indeed the feast of the Passover is placed either in the customary way at March 25th or, according to Epiphanius, at March 19th. We determine nothing for now, but leaving all things in the middle, we favor the opinion of Chemnitius very much.

VI. But especially the notation of time indicates the age of Christ, which alone Luke among all the Evangelists noted, namely that this baptism took place in the 30th year of his age from the assumption of human flesh, at which age also the Levitical priests were admitted to public ministries.

VII. But here again differing opinions occur, while some understand 30 completed years, others incomplete. Epiphanius affirms that Christ, when he was baptized, was 29 years and 10 months old: Jerome, exactly 30 years old: Chrysostom and others with him [say] he had exceeded the 30th year; others with Irenaeus establish the beginning of the 30th.

VIII. The words in Luke are thus: Jesus himself was beginning to be about 30 years old. A double sense, however, is attributed to these words. 1. By some the participle ἀρχόμενος is referred to the years, in this way: Christ, when he was baptized, was beginning to be about 30 years old. 2. Others attach the participle ἀρχόμενος not to the years, but to the public office or the beginning of his manifestation, in this sense: Jesus was beginning to declare himself to men, to teach, and to perform his duty, when he was born about 30 years old, beginning namely, to manifest and preach himself; which latter sense pleases the Jesuit Barradius in the said place, and he thinks it can be proven from Acts 1, v. 22 and chapter 10, 37. From this it is now clear in what year Christ was baptized, namely the 30th, but still current and incomplete, yet soon to be completed, for one or two months were perhaps still lacking. IX. But the madness of the Anabaptists is greatest, who, because of the example of Christ baptized in the 30th year of his age, think that baptism even now should be postponed, if not precisely to the 30th year, then certainly to the years of discretion, and therefore they abhor and execrate infant baptism. For besides the fact that the example of Christ is clearly singular and extraordinary, from which a general rule cannot be constructed without a divine mandate, this was the most important reason why Christ was not baptized in infancy, because baptism at that time had not yet been instituted, since it only began in the 29th year of his age under the ministry of the Baptist, which is not obscurely gathered from Luke 3, v. 2 and 3. Furthermore, Christ deferred baptism until his 30th year because there was no danger that he would be forestalled by death, a reason which expires in the case of infants. If, therefore, according to the dogma of the Anabaptists, baptism given to infants is not true baptism, it would follow that all those baptized in infant age did not receive true baptism, which is utterly absurd. X. Another circumstance contributing greatly to the confirmation of the event is the PLACE, which is the Jordan: for there John was baptizing at that time, and because of the abundance of water it was most suitable for baptism. This river is most well-known in Judea and at the same time most celebrated in Holy Scripture, especially because of the miracles that happened there: for through it the Israelites passed under the leadership of Joshua, proceeding from the desert into Palestine, Joshua 3, v. 16. Elijah, striking the Jordan with his mantle, divided it into two parts and crossed through the dry land with Elisha, 2 Kings 2, 8. In the same Jordan, Naaman the leper was healed when, according to the word of the man of GOD, he had previously washed in it seven times, 2 Kings 5, 14. XI. John the Evangelist expresses a more specific notation of the place, asserting that John was accustomed to baptize in Bethabara, which signifies the house of passage, that is, a place where one could cross either by a ford or by a boat. Hence some of the fathers think that John baptized at that place of the Jordan where the Israelites, after the Egyptian servitude, went out through the dry riverbed, where twelve stones taken from the middle of the Jordan's bed had been placed. These thoughts are certainly neither evil nor impious.

XII. From place and time we descend to the ministerial cause of Christ's baptism, which all the Evangelists record to have been John the Baptist, to whom alone it was granted both to announce Him while absent and to see Him while present. He did not devise the rite of baptism from his own brain, but began it by divine command. For thus it is written in Luke 3:2: the word of the Lord came to John, etc. And John 1:33, he himself confesses: He who sent me to baptize with water, He said to me, etc. Hence the baptism of John is said to have been from heaven and the counsel of God. Since, therefore, the baptism of John draws its origin from God, we cannot agree with those who formerly thought, and still think, that it was merely a bare ceremony destitute of all spiritual effect: for that this opinion is erroneous is easily evident from the cited passages.

XIII. But since Christ and John were raised in different places, and neither had associated familiarly with the other before the 30th year, therefore the Holy Spirit by a certain secret inspiration revealed to John that this Jesus was his Lord, of whom he himself was the precursor. Hence John was of such piety and humility that he would have prohibited Christ from approaching and seeking baptism, and, as if stupefied, burst forth into these words: I have need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me? For he deemed himself unworthy to baptize the Messiah. But having heard Christ's resolution, he desisted from his prohibition and most willingly admitted Him to baptism.

XIV. It is clearly credible that John performed this baptism not without singular exultation of the Spirit, both because Christ wished to use his ministry in fulfilling a part of righteousness, and because it was certain to him from the divine oracle in John 1:33 that the Messiah would be manifested in His baptism, namely through the miraculous descent of the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove, which also certainly followed, not when Christ and John were alone, but as Luke expressly mentions, when all the people were being baptized.

XV. Christ, therefore, having been baptized by John, not only approved the baptism of John by His own example, but also to the same he wished to procure some authority, because it was not from men, but from God.

XVI. Here the question arises, Was the baptism of John the same as the baptism of Christ, and consequently of all the ministers of the Church of Christ? Resp. That it was one and the same, and distinguished only by the ministerial efficient cause or even by some external circumstance, which nevertheless detracts nothing from the substance itself, namely that John baptized into Christ who was not far off from coming, but already coming or rather to be manifested: but the Apostles and the ministers of our Churches [baptize] into the same [Christ] already exhibited.

Latin:

VTi sacerdotes ac Levitæ in V. T. tabernaculum Domini ingressuri, manus priùs lavabant, qvàm in atrio sacris vacabant: ita verus & unicus Sacerdos N. T. Christus Jesus ministerium suum aggressurus, officiumqve redemptionis consummatus, per baptismi susceptionem eidem inaugurari voluit. Historiam autem baptismi Christi, de qvâ postulante ordinis ratione, DEO clementer adjuvante in præsentiâ dispiciendum, describit ἡ ἁγία τῶν εὐαγγελιῶν τετρακτὺς sacer qvaternio Evangeliorum Matth. 3, 13. Marc. 1, 9. Luc. 3, 21. Joh. 1, v. 29. & 32. qvamvis Evangelista Johanes alludendo saltem perstringat eam, videns procul dubio, ab aliis Evangelistis de illa satis superq́; literis esse proditum. Tametsi autem augusta planè & illustris hæc est historia, cujus singulæ circumstantiæ dignæ sunt, qvæ justâ diligentiâ considerentur, cùm propter exordium ministerii Christi, tùm etiam propter res gravissimas, qvæ in eâdem continentur, hac tamen vice ut scitu notatuq́; maximè necessaria excutiamus, qvinq; Capitula pensiculabimus, acturi 1. de Circumstantiis temporis ac loci. 2. De caussa ministeriali baptismum dispensante. 3. De ipso baptismi actu & miraculis eundē insecutis. 4. De caussa finali, cur Christus baptismum susceperit. 5. De succincta & pia hujus historiæ praxi.

Thesis I.

DUæ sunt circumstantiæ, teste Chytræo, qvibus certitudo veritatis historicæ demonstratur, nempe tempus & locus, operæ preciu itaq; fuerit, si nos qvoq; hâc in historiâ ad tempus & locum attendamus. Cùm verò circa tempus, qvâ diem, qvâ mensem mira opinionum ac supputationum se offerat varietas, ideò impræsentiarum adeò curiosi esse nolumus, ut Scripturâ duce & luce destituti certam aliqvam diei ac mensis determinationem annotare præsumamus, sed simplici opinionum qvarundam enarratione contenti, uno verbulo, cui sententiæ æqviores simus, aperiamus.

II. Qvidam postillatores (ita enim loqvitur Chemnitius) & Pontificii certū præcisumq; diem determinare nō dubitârunt, asserentes, Christum sexto Januarii die baptizatum, sed 1. absq; omni scripturæ fundamento: neq; enim Evangelistæ diem expressè annotârunt, neq; ex circumstantiis historiæ certò exactè & præcisè colligi potest. 2. Absq; omni vel probabili saltem ratione, nudam conjecturam duntaxat & incerta veterum traditione nixi.

III. Qvidam qvia Jordanis messis tempore omnes suas ripas implere consvevit, ut legitur Josuæ 3, 15. & Sirac. 24, 36. idcircò ante messem contigisse hunc baptismum autumant, tum temporis enim ripæ nondum fuerunt impletæ, siqvidem Christo & Johanni in Jordanem descendendum fuisse, in de probatur, quod Jesus baptizatus protinus ex aqva ascendisse dicitur.

IV. Alii putentes Johannem Baptistam ministerium suum inchoasse in ipso tubarum festo, hoc est, primo die septimi mensis, statuunt, Christum fuisse baptizatum decendio pòst in ipso expiationis festo, & sic verum propitiationis festum per Mosaicum obscurius adumbratum inchoâsse & celebrâsse. Unde qvidem elegantissima Viteris & Novi Testamenti analogia institui potest, licet hujus supputationis vestigia in historia Evangelica nullibi deprehendantur.

V. D. Chemnitius ex verisimilibus conjecturis tempus baptismi & ministerii exordium deducit ad principium Decembris vel ad finem Novembris, si nempe festum Paschatus ponatur vel usitato modo ad 25, Martii vel juxta Epiphanium ad 19. Martii. Nos nihil jam determinamus, sed omnia in medio reliqventes Chemnitii sententiae plurimum favemus.

VI. Cumprimis autem temporis notatio indicat aetatem Christi, qvam ex omnibus Evangelistis solus Lucas annotavit, quòd nempe hic baptismus per actus sit, anno aetatis 30. ab assumptione humanae carnis, qvâ in aetate etiam Levitici sacerdotes ad publica ministeria admissi sunt.

VII. Occurrunt autem hic iterum discrepantes opiniones, dum qvidam annos 30. completos intelligunt, qvidam incompletos. Epiphanius Christum, cùm baptisaretur 29. annorum & 10. mensium fuisse affirmat: Hiern. exactè 30. annorum: Chrysostomus aliiq; cum eo annum 30. excessisse; alii cum Irenaeo initium 30. constituunt.

VIII. Verba Luco sic habent: ipse Jesus erat incipiens fermè annorum 30. Duplex autem sensus attribuitur his verbis. 1. A nonnullis participium ἀρχόμενος refertur ad annos, hoc modo: Christus tunc cùm est baptizatus, annorum ferè 30. esse incipiebat. 2. Alii participium ἀρχόμενος non ad annos, sed ad officium publicum seu ostensionis exordium adjungum, hoc sensu: Erat Jesus incipiens se hominibus declarere, docere, & suum munus obire, cùm natus esset ferè annorum 30. superabat enim 29. annum, & aliqvid amplius adhuc, quasi dicat Lucas, Erat Jesus incipiens quasi 30. annorum, incipiens scilicet, se aliis manifestare & prædicare; qvi posterior sensus magis placet Barradio Jesuitæ d. l. & probari posse censet ex Act. 1. v. 22. & cap. 10, 37. Hinc jam constat, qvoto anno Christus baptisatus sit, nempe 30. sed adhuc curente & incompleto, brevi tamen complendo, unus enim & alter mensis adhuc fortasse abfuit. IX. Vesania autem maxima est Anabatistarum, qvi ob exemplum Christi anno ætatis 30. baptizatis, etiamnum baptismum, si non præcisè in annum 30. at certè in annos discretionis procrastinandum censet, atq; idcircò Pædobaptismum abominantur & execrantur. Præterqvam enim, qvod exemplum Christi planè singulare est & extraordinarium, ex qvo sine divino mandato regula generalis extrui neqvit, hæc potissima erat caussa, qvòd Christus in infantia non est baptizatus, qvia baptismus tum temporis nondum erat institutus, qvippe qvi cœpit demum anno ætatis 29. sub ministerio Baptistæ, id qvod non obscurè colligitur ex Luc. 3. v. 2. & 3. Deinde Christus baptismum distulit usqve ad annum 30. qvia non erat periculum, ne præveniretur morte, qvæ ratio in infantibus expirat. Si itaqve juxta Anabaptistarum dogma baptismus datus infantibus, non est verus baptismus, seqveretur, omnes in ætate infantili baptizatos non accepisse verum baptismum, id qvod oppidò absurdum. X. Altera circumstantia ad confirmationem rei gestæ plurimùm faciens est LOCUS, qvi Jordanis: Nam ibi Johannes tum temporis baptizabat, & propter aqvarum affluentiam baptismo erat accommodatissimus. Fluvius hic in Judæa est notissimus & in Scriptura sacra simul celebratissimus, cumprimis ob miracula, qvæ in isto acciderunt: per hunc enim Israëlitæ transiverunt duce Josua è deserto pergentes in Palæstinam, Josuæ 3. v. 16. Elias pallio Jordanem percutiens in duas partes eum divisit, & per siccum cum Elisæ transiit, 2. Reg. 2, 8. Eodem in Jordane Naaman leprosus sanatus est, cùm juxta verbum viri DEI prius in eodem septies lavisset, 2. Reg. 5, 14. XI. Johannes Evangelista specialiorem loci notationem exprimit, asserens, qvòd Johannes solitus sit baptizare in Bethabara, qvæ domum transitus significat, hoc est, locum, ubi trajici potuit vel vado vel navigio. Hinc qvidam ex patribus sentiunt, Johannem eo Jordanis loco baptizasse, qvo Israëlitæ post servitudem Ægyptiacam per arentem fluminis alveum egressi sunt, ubi duodecim lapides de medio Jordanis alveo sublati, fuerant collicati. Qvæ sanè cogitationes nec malæ sunt, nec impiæ.

XII. A loco & tempore descendimus ad caussam ministerialem baptismi Christi, qvam omnes Evangelistæ memorant, fuisse Johannem baptistam, cui soli concessum fuit & prænunciare absentem & videre præsentem. Is baptisationis ritum de suo cerebro non excogitavit, sed divino mandato eum inchoavit. Sic enim scriptum Luc. 3, 2. factum est verbum Domini ad Johannem &c. Et Joh. 1, 33. ipse fatetur, qui misit me, ut baptizarem aqvâ, is dixit mihi &c. Hinc baptismus Johannis dicitur fuisse de cœlo & consilium DEI. Cum itaq; baptismus Johannis suam à DEO ducat originem, non possumus facere cum illis qvi olim putârunt & adhuc putant, eum fuisse nudam duntaxat ceremoniam omni effectu spirituali destitutam: nam qvòd hæc opinio erronea sit, ex allegatis dictis facilè patescit.

XIII. Qvoniam verò Christus & Johannes diversis in locis educati sunt, nec alter cum altero ante annum 30. familiariter conversatus fuerat, idcirco Spiritus sanctus inspiratione qvâdam arcanâ revelavit Johanni, hunc Jesum esse Dominum suum, cujus ipse præcursor esset. Hinc tantæ pietatis & humilitatis erat Johannes, ut Christum adventantem baptismumq; petentem prohiberet & obstupefactus qvasi in hæc verba erumperet, Ego opus habeo, ut abs te baptizer, & ut venis ad me: se enim indignum est ratus, qvi Messiam baptizaret. Auditâ verò Christi resolutione à prohibitione destitit, & ad baptismum lubentissimè admisit.

XIV. Planè autem credibile est, qvòd Johannes hunc baptismum peregerit non absq; singulari Spiritus exultatione, tum qvia in implendâ parte justitiæ Christus ministerio suo uti voluit, tum qvia ex divino Oraculo Joh. 1. v. 33. eidem constabat, fore ut Messias in baptismo suo manifestaretur, nempe per miraculosam Spiritus sancti in specie columbæ descensionem, qvæ etiam certò subsecuta fuit, non cùm soli essent Christus & Johannes, sed uti Lucas expressè meminit, cùm omnis populus baptisaretur.

XV. Christus itaq; baptisatus à Johanne proprio suo exemplo non solùm comprobavit baptismum Johannis, verùm etiam eidem autoritatem aliqvam conciliare voluit, qvòd non ex hominibus, sed ex Deo esset.

XVI. Hîc incidit qvæstio, An babtismus Johannis idem fuerit cum Christi, apostolorum adeog, omnium Ecclesiæ Christi ministrorum baptisma? Resp. Unum & eundem fuisse, nec nisi ministeriali efficiente causâ vel etiam externâ qvâdam circumstantiâ distinctum, qvæ tamen ipsi substantiæ nihil detrahit, nempe Johannes baptisavit in Christum & non longè venturum, sed jam venientem vel potiùs manifestandum: Apostoli verò & nostrarum Ecclesiarum ministri in eundem exhibitum.


### XVII. For they agree 1

XVII. For they agree 1. In the efficient cause or first author, who is God: 2. In the common mandate received from God. 3. In the matter or element, which is water. 4. In the formula of baptizing. 5.
